sources.note: Phonology is of BARANG-BARANG (sister language, 77% lexically similar): sec. 11 'Word stress', p.60: 'Word stress is normally penultimate. This applies to roots as well as derived forms', with antepenultimate stress in recent loans carrying an epenthetic echo-vowel -V? syllable. On Kalao itself, p.46: 'No published language data exists for Kalao'. Appendix A (pp.65-74) gives a 488-item Kalao wordlist with no stress marking (checked page image p-20).

sources.citation: [Anonymous to this searcher -- author/title page not verified] Article on the island of Saleijer (Selayar) and its dependencies (Bonerate, Kalaoe/Lambego, Tana-Djampeija), in Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indie, 1880s volume digitised by Google as archive.org item 'bijdragentotdet10unkngoog' (passages at printed pp. c.276, 292, 372, 400-401).
sources.note: No phonology content. Only a classificatory remark: 'Een feit is het, dat de taal, gesproken in de zuidelijke regentschappen, zoo niet dezelfde is, minstens zeer veel overeenkomst bezit met die der eilanden Kalaoe of Lambego en Bonerate, geheel afwijkende van het Saleijereesch, meer nog van het Makassaarsch en Boegineesch' (p. c.400) -- i.e. the speech of Layolo/Barang-Barang/Bontoboroso resembles that of Kalao/Lambego and Bonerate. Full djvu text was downloaded to the work dir, a full-text search for stress/accent Lambego/taal/klemtoon/accent, then deleted.
